08-deadlines.mp3: A TA claim for tour, transfer or training normally must be submitted
within 60 days after the journey; a late claim may be forfeited,
For example, if the journey ends on 1 October 2026, then
2 October is day one and 30 November is day 60.
Submit on time to the correct office and keep proof.
For retirement TA, the 2021 order set a limit of 180 days
after the journey; tour, transfer and training remain at 60 days.
For example, if an eligible retirement journey ends on 1 October 2026,
Remember: the period allowed to make a journey and the claim-filing deadline
are different. The guide discusses possible review of old unsettled cases.
09-submission.mp3: If an employee and family travel separately on transfer,
the claim clock starts separately for each journey.
For example, the employee arrives on 1 October and the family on 11 October;
their completion dates are counted separately.
For personal effects or conveyance, separately check the actual delivery
When a claim is considered submitted also depends on whether
you are your own controlling officer.
If not, check the submission date to the Head of Office or controlling officer;
if you are your own controlling officer, check the presentation date
at the Treasury or Cash Section.
For example, you submit to your controlling officer on day 45,
and Treasury receives it later: subject to the order's conditions,
the earlier submission date may matter.
Keep the receipt or acknowledgement safe.
10-boarding-pass.mp3: Quick official update: what if a boarding pass is missing? The 2020 DoE
order applies to official tour journeys by Central Government employees.
If neither a physical nor a digital copy is available, the prescribed declaration
may be submitted with the TA bill.
For example, a Level 9 employee loses the pass and declares the actual journey,
PNR details and that the claim is not duplicated.
Employees at Level 10 and below must have the declaration
This missing-pass declaration differs from the journey-completion certificate. The June
2022 order requires the completion certificate within 72
hours of the journey; the TA bill is submitted later under separate rules.
For example, an employee sends the completion certificate after a flight. If the
boarding pass is missing, they attach the separate prescribed declaration to the bill.
A false declaration may lead to disciplinary action and recovery.
